description:
FILED s470bv (Opus, 2026-09-06) while attributing the s470br batch's companion
movers.  MEASURED, not inferred.

THE NUMBERS (tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1, each in its own worktree):

    614c6af   (before the s470 batches)   C 4/11   passing rows {3,5,6,9}
    3a89a5c   (#1115 + review fixes)      C 2/13   passing rows {8,9}
    b25afbc   (#1221)                     C 3/12   passing rows {4,8,9}
    424cabc / HEAD                        C 3/12   passing rows {4,8,9}

perl runs 15 rows; PCL passes 3.

WHAT THE ROWS TEST.  t/run/switchC.t is entirely about perl's `-C` command-line
switch (and the PERL_UNICODE environment variable it mirrors): -CI (decode
STDIN), -CO (encode STDOUT), -CE (encode STDERR), -Ci / -Co (the implicit
`use open` layers for input/output), -CS, -CA (@ARGV), -CL (locale gating), and
the "has file scope" rules.  PCL implements NONE of it: the switch is not
parsed by ./runpcl or tools/pclperl-for-tests, and there is no runtime hook.

WHY THREE ROWS USED TO PASS.  Before #1115 PCL decoded every handle by default,
i.e. `-C` was permanently ON by accident, so `-CI`, `-Co` and `-Ci` "worked".
#1115 made the default BYTES (perl's own default), which is right, and those
three rows became honest failures; the same change made row 8 (`-Ci ... has
file scope`, an `unlike`) start passing, because bytes IS the right answer
without the switch.  #1221 (`utf8::encode` really transforms) then made row 4
(`-CE: UTF-8 stderr`) pass, because the file's own
`my $b = chr 256; utf8::encode $b;` now produces the two octets the expected
output carries.

So the snapshot move 4/11 -> 3/12 is HONEST in both directions and is spliced
with that cause; this task owns the remaining 12.

SCOPE / SIZE.  Real work, not a filler: the switch has to be read at startup
(both by `pcl`/`runpcl` and by `tools/pclperl-for-tests`, which is what the
suite's child programs run under), turn into the same layer facts #1224's
grammar already produces, and apply to the three std handles plus the implicit
`use open` defaults -- with perl's "file scope" rule for -Ci/-Co.  PERL_UNICODE
is the same table.  Do it AFTER #1270 (the compile-time `use open` reader),
because -Ci/-Co are defined in terms of exactly that mechanism.

ACCEPTANCE: t/run/switchC.t 3/12 -> 15/0, or every remaining row explained;
guard rows in Pl/t asserting -CI/-CO/-CE/-Ci/-Co and PERL_UNICODE.
subject: The `-C` command-line switch is implemented NOWHERE in PCL: t/run/switchC.t has 12 failing rows, and its three passing `-CI`/`-Co`/`-Ci` rows before #1115 were an ACCIDENT of PCL decoding everything by default
